2 عسّل الطَّعَامَ , inf. n. تَعْسِيلٌ: see 1, first sentence. ―
-b2- عَسَّلْتُهُمْ, (S, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, O,) I furnished them with عَسَل [i. e. honey] for travelling-provision; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ عَسَلْتُهُمْ . (K.) ―
-b3- And عسّل الرَّجُلَ, inf. n. as above, He made the man's condiment to be عَسَل [or honey]. (TA.) ―
-b4- And the Arabs say, عَسِّلُوا ضَيْفَكُمْ, meaning Divert ye your guest with something [whereby to allay the craving of his stomach] before the [morning-meal called] غَدَآء; like لَمِّجُوهُ and لَهِّجُوهُ &c. (El-Umawee, TA in art. لهج.) ―
-b5- And عَسَّلَتِ النَّحْلُ The bees made honey. (TA.) ―
-b6- [And, accord. to Freytag, عسّل signifies He collected honey: but for this he names no authority.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
